lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
lessonRef.title: Application or project: building a plate with variety

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 4: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice building a plate with variety. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult and the learner are preparing a real meal or snack together.
safetyNotes: Check with your household adult before handling any food-prep tools, hot surfaces, or the stove or oven; plate-building itself does not require them.
Only use foods your household adult says are available and appropriate for you to handle.
Wash your hands before touching any food for the plate.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real meal or snack is being prepared during this lesson, the learner instead sketches a picture of a real meal from the household's kitchen, from memory or by looking in the refrigerator or pantry without preparing anything, labels the food groups, colors, and textures they see, then writes what they would add to increase variety.

materials: adult-or-local: a real meal or snack being prepared in the household
adult-or-local: a trusted adult present nearby

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain one specific way you could add even more variety to this same plate next time, using the food groups, colors, or textures you noticed were missing.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Variety planning and execution: The plan and the actual plate each include at least three food groups, two colors, and two textures. | Comparison and next step: The comparison names specific differences and rates the overall variety accurately. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner plan and compare a second plate at a different meal or snack later in the day, then compare which of the two plates achieved more variety and what made the difference.

resources.title: building a plate with variety worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult and the learner are preparing a real meal or snack together.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact building a plate with variety decision or action.
Model move 2: Before planning, look at what food is actually available for this meal or snack today.
Model move 3: Using only the foods actually available, sketch a quick plan for your plate.

Model check: Variety planning and execution: The plan and the actual plate each include at least three food groups, two colors, and two textures. | Comparison and next step: The comparison names specific differences and rates the overall variety accurately.

resources.title: building a plate with variety action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for building a plate with variety.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-guided-card.

resources.title: building a plate with variety coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult and the learner are preparing a real meal or snack together.
Coach direction: Before planning, look at what food is actually available for this meal or snack today.
Learner prompt: List the foods available for this meal or snack, and name which food group each one belongs to (grains, fruits, vegetables, protein, or dairy).
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: building a plate with variety complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using only the foods actually available, sketch a quick plan for your plate. Aim for at least three different food groups, at least two different colors, and at least two different textures, like something crunchy and something soft.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My plan includes foods from at least three different food groups.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My plan includes at least two different colors.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My plan includes at least two different textures.

Equal-access rule: If no real meal or snack is being prepared during this lesson, the learner instead sketches a picture of a real meal from the household's kitchen, from memory or by looking in the refrigerator or pantry without preparing anything, labels the food groups, colors, and textures they see, then writes what they would add to increase variety.

resources.title: building a plate with variety minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific way you could add even more variety to this same plate next time, using the food groups, colors, or textures you noticed were missing.

Success checks: Variety planning and execution: The plan and the actual plate each include at least three food groups, two colors, and two textures. | Comparison and next step: The comparison names specific differences and rates the overall variety accurately.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: building a plate with variety supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional building a plate with variety condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Variety planning and execution: The plan and the actual plate each include at least three food groups, two colors, and two textures. | Comparison and next step: The comparison names specific differences and rates the overall variety accurately..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
